raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Cut the CPU an API server spends turning a finished request's logprobs into the HTTP response: validate the generate endpoint's logprob tree in one pydantic-core pass, serialize the non-streaming generate, chat and completions responses with `model_dump_json()`, and take the chat logprob models off the request-side extra-field validator. Same wire format, no new options. Follows #58181, which did the equivalent for the generate endpoint's models, and the `Response` shape suggested in #33548.

## Claims

- With the default single API server and `logprobs=8`, generation throughput rises 21–23% on `/inference/v1/generate` and 9–11% on `/v1/chat/completions` (`top_logprobs=8`), on R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, Qwen3-4B and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, one H100, two trials each with no overlap.
- With `--api-server-count 8` throughput is unchanged (±2%) and API-server CPU per generated token falls 12–23% at `logprobs=8`.
- The synchronous block per finished 620-token response shrinks 1.7x on generate (20.4 to 12.1 µs per token at k=8) and 1.6x on chat (35.4 to 21.6 µs), build and serialization included. Response bytes are identical; the only behavioral difference is that a NaN float in a response would serialize as `null` instead of failing the request, and the logprob fields are already clamped.

## Validation

Load: 768 chat-templated prompts from `sail/Sanity-Test-R1D-1.5B`, 256 in flight, `max_tokens` uniform in 128–1024, temperature 1, `top_p=0.95`, `top_k=512`, `logprobs=k`. Server: `vllm serve <model> --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 4096 --logprobs-mode processed_logprobs --generation-config vllm --max-logprobs 20 --return-sampling-mask --enable-scale-out --api-server-count {1,8}`, one H100 and 11 CPUs per job, main at f98ae6a9 vs this branch in the same venv. Client and microbenchmark: [bench.py](https://github.com/AmineDiro/vllm/blob/assets/logprob-responses/logprob-responses/bench.py), [micro.py](https://github.com/AmineDiro/vllm/blob/assets/logprob-responses/logprob-responses/micro.py).

Single API server, generated tokens/s, main → PR:

| model | generate k=0 | generate k=8 | chat `top_logprobs=8` |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B | 16.7k → 18.2k (+9%) | 6.9k → 8.5k (+23%) | 5.2k → 5.8k (+11%) |
| Qwen3-4B | 13.6k → 13.8k (+2%) | 6.5k → 7.9k (+21%) | 5.0k → 5.5k (+9%) |
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct | 13.3k → 14.4k (+8%) | 6.8k → 8.3k (+22%) | 5.2k → 5.7k (+11%) |

![throughput](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmineDiro/vllm/assets/logprob-responses/logprob-responses/throughput.png)

Eight API servers, API-server CPU in µs per generated token, main → PR (throughput within ±2% in every cell):

| model | generate k=0 | generate k=4 | generate k=8 | chat `top_logprobs=8` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B | 31 → 29 | 53 → 48 | 80 → 67 | 100 → 89 |
| Qwen3-4B | 37 → 34 | 63 → 54 | 90 → 76 | 117 → 97 |
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct | 33 → 31 | 56 → 51 | 81 → 70 | 101 → 78 |

<details>
<summary>Profile, microbenchmark and CPU figures</summary>

py-spy on the single API server at k=8, R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, categories by the first matching frame from the leaf (GC pauses are charged to the allocating frame, which is why the per-step categories grow slightly):

![profile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmineDiro/vllm/assets/logprob-responses/logprob-responses/profile.png)

One finished 620-token response, µs per generated token, login-node CPU, median of 15 (`micro.py`, which also asserts the route bytes are unchanged):

![micro](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmineDiro/vllm/assets/logprob-responses/logprob-responses/micro.png)

![api_cpu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AmineDiro/vllm/assets/logprob-responses/logprob-responses/api_cpu.png)

</details>

Tests, on the branch: `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/{test_tokens_logprobs,test_protocol,test_serving_tokens}.py`, `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/{test_generate_logprobs_conversion,test_logprobs_endpoint_parity}.py`, `tests/entrypoints/openai/test_return_tokens_as_ids.py`, `tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion.py -k logprob`, `tests/entrypoints/openai/test_chunked_prompt.py`, `tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/{test_chat.py -k logprob,test_logprob_token_ids,test_chat_echo,test_batched_chat_completions.py -k logprob,test_chat_completion}.py` all pass (one H100). No new tests: the existing ones check the values and shapes these methods produce, and the microbenchmark asserts byte equality of the route output.

## Details

With `logprobs=k`, finishing a request makes the API server build `k + 1` pydantic objects per generated token, dump them to dicts and encode the dicts with the stdlib encoder, in one synchronous block on the event loop (12.6 ms for a 620-token response at k=8 on main). py-spy on a single API server at k=8 puts 40% of its active time in that block, which is why `logprobs=8` costs 50–60% of throughput there while eight API servers hide it.

- `_create_tokens_logprobs` builds plain dicts and calls `GenerateLogProbs.model_validate` once: pydantic-core validates the whole tree without a Python-level `__init__` per candidate. `model_construct` is slower (it is Python), and `TypedDict` entries would be faster still but change the Python-side types derender and the tests use.
- `_clamp_logprob` is one comparison instead of `math.isnan` plus `max`; NaN compares False, so NaN and `-inf` still map to `-9999.0`. It was the top self-time frame of the profile (15%) because it runs once per candidate.
- The three non-streaming routes return `Response(content=generator.model_dump_json(), media_type="application/json")`: no intermediate dict tree, no stdlib encoder. `model_dump_json` was 2.5x faster than `model_dump` + `json.dumps` and faster than `orjson.dumps(model_dump())`, which still builds the tree. Error responses and streaming are untouched.
- `ChatCompletionLogProb*` were `OpenAIBaseModel`, whose `__log_extra_fields__` wrap validator checks a request dict for unknown fields; on these response-only objects it only cost time, and it is what required the `field_names` cache workaround from #13925, now removed. `extra="allow"` is kept.

Not changed here: candidate detokenization in tokens mode (`LogprobsProcessor` decodes text the generate endpoint never sends, about 8% of the same profile) and the per-step `Logprob` objects; both are engine-output-path changes.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>
